props.gloss_en: one who forgets the essence of Shabbat and did many labours on many Shabbatot is liable only one chatat
one who knows the essence of Shabbat and did many labours on many Shabbatot is liable for each Shabbat
one who knows that it is Shabbat and did many labours on many Shabbatot is liable for each primary labour
Rav and Shmuel: our mishna [one who forgets the essence of Shabbat] is a child captured among the gentiles and a convert who converted among the gentiles
Rav and Shmuel: but one who knew and in the end forgot is liable for each Shabbat
rather, our mishna is [speaking of] one who knew and in the end forgot
a child captured among the gentiles and a convert among the gentiles are like one who knew and in the end forgot
Rav and Shmuel (as והכי איתמר reports them): and [the captured child and the convert] are liable
R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish: [liable] specifically one who knew and in the end forgot
a child captured among the gentiles and a convert among the gentiles are exempt (R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish; and Munbaz in the baraita)
the baraita: how so? a child captured among the gentiles or a convert among the gentiles who did many labours on many Shabbatot is liable only one chatat
the baraita: and he is liable one [chatat] for blood, one for forbidden fat, and one for idolatry
Munbaz: since the deliberate sinner is called 'sinner' and the unwitting one is called 'sinner', as the deliberate one had knowledge, so the unwitting one [is liable only if he] had knowledge

R' Akiva's addition, which Munbaz accepts ('yes, and all the more so now that you have added'): as the deliberate one had knowledge at the time of the act, so the unwitting one had knowledge at the time of the act
the Rabbis need 'one law' (Num 15:29) for what R' Yehoshua ben Levi read to his son
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: every matter whose deliberate violation carries karet -- for its unwitting violation one is liable a chatat
for Munbaz, being unwitting about the offering [alone] counts as shegaga
for the Rabbis, being unwitting about the offering is not called shegaga
R' Yochanan: [it is shegaga] once he was unwitting about the karet, even though he was deliberate about the prohibition
Reish Lakish: [it is not shegaga] until he is unwitting about the prohibition and the karet
Rava: Reish Lakish's reason is the verse 'which may not be done, unwittingly, and is guilty' (Lev 4:27) -- until he is unwitting about the prohibition and its karet
R' Yochanan needs Reish Lakish's verse for the baraita (R' Shimon's derasha: one who would turn back on learning brings an offering)
the baraita: 'from the people of the land' (Lev 4:27) -- to exclude an apostate
R' Shimon: 'which may not be done, unwittingly, and is guilty' -- one who would turn back on learning [of his sin] brings an offering for his error; one who would not turn back does not

schemas.gloss_en: 'one law for the one who acts unwittingly' (Num 15:29) is adjacent to 'the soul that acts with a high hand' (Num 15:30): He juxtaposed unwitting to deliberate -- as the deliberate had knowledge, so the unwitting had knowledge

'one law' (Num 15:29), 'and if you err and do not do all these commandments' (Num 15:22), 'the soul that acts with a high hand' (Num 15:30): all were juxtaposed to idolatry -- as there, a matter whose deliberate violation is karet and whose unwitting violation is a chatat, so every such matter

supports.gloss_en: וכך היה מונבז דן לפני רבי עקיבא -- the unwitting sinner, like the deliberate, is liable only with prior knowledge; the captured child had none
מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון בן לקיש -- אמר קרא: אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם (Lev 4:27) (a verse adduced; no SupportKind names one)
מיבעי ליה לכדתניא -- the baraita's derasha (R' Shimon via R' Shimon ben Elazar) is what the verse is spent on for R' Yochanan (no SupportKind names כדתניא)

objections.gloss_en: תנן: השוכח עיקר שבת -- לאו מכלל דהויא ליה ידיעה מעיקרא? -- 'one who FORGETS' implies he once knew, which a captured child never did

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, מאי השוכח עיקר שבת -- שהיתה שכוחה ממנו עיקרה של שבת: the essence of Shabbat was [always] forgotten from him

objections.gloss_en: אבל הכיר ולבסוף שכח מאי -- חייב על כל שבת ושבת? אדתני היודע עיקר שבת... ליתני הכיר ולבסוף שכח, וכל שכן הא -- if one who knew and forgot is liable for each Shabbat, the mishna should have taught that case, and the one who knows a fortiori

answered_by.gloss_en: מאי היודע עיקר שבת -- מי שהיה יודע עיקרה של שבת ושכחה: 'one who knows the essence' IS one who knew it and forgot it

objections.gloss_en: אבל לא שכחה מאי -- חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה? אדתני היודע שהוא שבת... ליתני היודע עיקר שבת, וכל שכן הא -- then the mishna's third clause is the wrong one to teach; אלא מתניתין כשהכיר ולבסוף שכח
the same move (68b.1): it defeats the re-reading that answered 68a.9, and the mishna's one-chatat case becomes the one who knew and forgot -- so he is not liable for each Shabbat
מיתיבי (68b.2) ... קתני מיהא כיצד תינוק: בשלמא לרב ושמואל ניחא, אלא לרבי יוחנן ולרבי שמעון בן לקיש קשיא -- the baraita has the captured child liable one chatat

answered_by.gloss_en: אמרי לך ר' יוחנן ור"ל: לא מי איכא מונבז דפטר? אנן דאמרינן כמונבז -- we said ours in accordance with Munbaz

objections.gloss_en: לדבריך, אין זה קרוי שוגג אלא מזיד -- by your words, one with knowledge at the time of the act is not called unwitting but deliberate

answered_by.gloss_en: ואלא מונבז שגגה במאי? כגון ששגג בקרבן -- for Munbaz the error is about the offering (see header: judgement call)
